title: Junior Software Engineer - Behavioral
persona: Friendly startup engineering manager. Casual but professional tone.

questions.text: Tell me a little about yourself and why you're interested in this role.
Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate. How did you handle it?
Tell me about a project you're proud of. What was your role and the outcome?
How do you handle tight deadlines or pressure?

title: Mid-Level Software Engineer - Technical
persona: Direct, precise senior engineer running a technical screen.

questions.text: Walk me through how you would design a simple URL-shortening service.
What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases, and when would you choose each?
How do you approach debugging a production issue you can't reproduce locally?
Explain a time you improved the performance of a system. What was the bottleneck?
Imagine a campaign you launched is underperforming a week before the deadline. What do you do?
How would you prioritize between three marketing requests due the same day?
Tell me about a time you used data to change your approach to a project.
How do you stay current with marketing trends and channels?

title: Senior Financial Analyst - Behavioral
persona: Formal, composed finance director in a corporate setting.

questions.text: Describe a time your financial analysis changed a business decision.
Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex financial result to a non-finance audience.
How do you ensure accuracy under a tight month-end close deadline?
Describe a situation where you identified a financial risk before it became a problem.

title: Junior Software Engineer - Programming Fundamentals
persona: Patient, friendly senior developer running a junior technical screen.

questions.text: Describe the principles of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP).
questions.referenceAnswer: OOP principles include encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction, promoting organized and maintainable code.

questions.text: What is the difference between an array and a linked list?
questions.referenceAnswer: An array has fixed size and stores elements in contiguous memory; a linked list consists of nodes with data and references, allowing dynamic size.

questions.text: Explain the concept of recursion.
questions.referenceAnswer: Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve subproblems, with a base case to terminate recursion.

questions.text: What is a merge conflict, and how do you resolve it in Git?
questions.referenceAnswer: Merge conflicts occur when changes in different branches clash. Resolve by manually editing files and committing the result.

questions.text: What is unit testing, and why is it important?
questions.referenceAnswer: Unit testing evaluates individual code components, ensuring correctness and facilitating early defect detection.

title: Junior Web Developer - Web Basics
persona: Encouraging front-end lead checking core web knowledge.

questions.text: Describe the differences between GET and POST requests.
questions.referenceAnswer: GET requests retrieve data and include parameters in the URL; POST requests send data to the server, encapsulating data in the request body.

questions.text: Explain the difference between HTTP and HTTPS.
questions.referenceAnswer: HTTP is an unsecured data transmission protocol; HTTPS is secure, encrypting data in transit using SSL/TLS.

questions.text: What is a cookie, and how does it work?
questions.referenceAnswer: Cookies are data stored on the user's computer by the web server, sent with HTTP requests for session management, tracking, and storing preferences.

questions.text: Explain the concept of responsive web design.
questions.referenceAnswer: Responsive design ensures web content functions across different devices and screen sizes, using CSS media queries and flexible layouts.

questions.text: What is a RESTful API?
questions.referenceAnswer: RESTful API is a web service implementation using HTTP methods to perform CRUD operations on resources, adhering to stateless, client-server architecture.

questions.text: Describe how you would implement a RESTful API in a back-end application.
questions.referenceAnswer: A RESTful API is implemented by setting up HTTP routes (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and handling requests and responses in a stateless manner, often using JSON.

questions.text: What is a database index, and why is it important?
questions.referenceAnswer: A database index speeds up data retrieval, similar to a book's index, improving query performance.

questions.text: Describe the ACID properties in database transactions.
questions.referenceAnswer: ACID: Atomicity (indivisible transactions), Consistency (consistent state transitions), Isolation (independent transactions), Durability (persisted changes).

questions.text: What is a 'race condition' in software development?
questions.referenceAnswer: A race condition occurs when the system's behavior depends on the sequence or timing of other uncontrollable events.

questions.text: How do NoSQL databases handle data scaling compared to traditional SQL databases?
questions.referenceAnswer: NoSQL databases are generally more scalable and provide superior performance for large-scale applications due to their flexibility in handling unstructured data.

questions.text: Explain the concept of 'closure' in JavaScript.
questions.referenceAnswer: A closure is a function that remembers its outer variables and can access them.

questions.text: Can you explain the concept of 'state' in React?
questions.referenceAnswer: State in React is an object that holds some information that may change over the lifecycle of the component.

questions.text: Explain the use of hooks in React.
questions.referenceAnswer: Hooks are functions that let you 'hook into' React state and lifecycle features from function components.

questions.text: What are the benefits of server-side rendering vs client-side rendering?
questions.referenceAnswer: Server-side rendering improves initial page load time and SEO, while client-side rendering is good for dynamic websites with less initial loading content.

questions.text: How would you optimize a website's load time?
questions.referenceAnswer: Optimizations can include minimizing HTTP requests, using CDNs, compressing files, caching, etc.

questions.text: What is Docker, and how does it work?
questions.referenceAnswer: Docker is a containerization platform packaging applications with dependencies, ensuring consistent environments across systems.

questions.text: What is continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD)?
questions.referenceAnswer: CI involves frequent code integration and testing; CD extends CI by deploying changes to production automatically after testing.

questions.text: What is Blue-Green deployment, and when would you use it?
questions.referenceAnswer: Blue-Green deployment alternates between two production environments for easy rollbacks and minimal downtime during updates.

questions.text: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)?
questions.referenceAnswer: IaC manages infrastructure using code, ensuring consistency, automation, and version control in deployments.

questions.text: How do you monitor the performance of a web application?
questions.referenceAnswer: Monitor using tools to collect and analyze data on response times, resource utilization, error rates, and user experience.

questions.text: What is SQL injection, and how can it be prevented?
questions.referenceAnswer: SQL injection exploits vulnerabilities to execute malicious SQL. Prevent with parameterized queries, input validation, and least privilege access.

questions.text: Explain the concept of Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
questions.referenceAnswer: XSS injects malicious scripts into web apps, executed by users' browsers. Prevent with input validation, output encoding, and CSP.

questions.text: Describe the process of password hashing and salting.
questions.referenceAnswer: Hashing transforms passwords into hashes using algorithms; salting adds randomness, enhancing security against attacks.

questions.text: What is OAuth, and how does it work?
questions.referenceAnswer: OAuth allows third-party app access to user data without exposing credentials, using access tokens for authorization.

questions.text: What is a DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attack?
questions.referenceAnswer: A DDoS attack overwhelms a target with traffic, causing unavailability. Mitigate with DDoS protection, rate limiting, and traffic analysis.

title: Mid-Level Software Engineer - Engineering Practices
persona: Thoughtful engineering manager who cares about code quality.

questions.text: Describe the purpose of code reviews.
questions.referenceAnswer: Code reviews identify defects, improve quality, enforce standards, and facilitate knowledge sharing.

questions.text: Explain the concept of code coverage in testing.
questions.referenceAnswer: Code coverage measures the extent of code tested, assessing test thoroughness and identifying untested areas.

questions.text: What is code refactoring, and why is it important?
questions.referenceAnswer: Refactoring improves code structure and readability without altering functionality, enhancing maintainability and quality.

questions.text: What is Git rebase, and when would you use it?
questions.referenceAnswer: Git rebase re-applies commits onto another base for a cleaner history. Use with caution to maintain a linear project history.

questions.text: Explain the difference between black-box and white-box testing.
questions.referenceAnswer: Black-box tests functionality without internal code knowledge; white-box tests internal code logic and structure.

title: Mid-Level Software Engineer - System Design Basics
persona: Calm, curious staff engineer who likes reasoning about trade-offs.

questions.text: Discuss the pros and cons of monolithic vs. microservices architecture.
questions.referenceAnswer: Monolithic is simple but less scalable; microservices offer scalability and flexibility but are complex to manage.

questions.text: What is a load balancer, and why is it used in web applications?
questions.referenceAnswer: A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across servers, ensuring resource efficiency, fault tolerance, and high availability.

questions.text: Explain the importance of caching in web applications.
questions.referenceAnswer: Caching stores frequently accessed data for faster retrieval, reducing backend load, improving performance, and enhancing user experience.

questions.text: What is a message broker, and when would you use one?
questions.referenceAnswer: A message broker facilitates communication in distributed systems through asynchronous messaging, used in event-driven architectures and high-volume scenarios.

questions.text: What is a CDN (Content Delivery Network)?
questions.referenceAnswer: A CDN is a network of servers for delivering content efficiently to users based on geographic proximity, reducing latency and load times.

title: Senior Software Engineer - System Design
persona: Experienced principal engineer running a design round.

questions.text: Design a chat application that can scale to millions of users.
questions.referenceAnswer: Consider websocket protocol for real-time communication, efficient message broadcasting, and scalable backend architecture.

questions.text: Design a scalable notification system for a social network.
questions.referenceAnswer: Focus on system architecture, push vs. pull models, handling peak loads, database optimization, and message queuing.

questions.text: Design an API rate limiter for a web service.
questions.referenceAnswer: Use token bucket or leaky bucket algorithms, consider distributed storage for scalability.

questions.text: Design a distributed key-value store.
questions.referenceAnswer: Focus on data partitioning, replication for fault tolerance, consistency models, and handling node failures.

questions.text: Design a global video streaming service like Netflix.
questions.referenceAnswer: Focus on CDN usage, adaptive bitrate streaming, content caching strategies, and handling peak traffic loads.

questions.text: Explain the concept of CAP theorem in distributed systems.
questions.referenceAnswer: The CAP theorem states that in a distributed system, you cannot simultaneously guarantee Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance at all times.

questions.text: How do you ensure data consistency in a distributed database?
questions.referenceAnswer: Ensure consistency using strong consistency models, two-phase commits, optimistic concurrency control, and conflict resolution strategies.

questions.text: Explain the Raft consensus algorithm.
questions.referenceAnswer: Discuss leader election, log replication, safety, and how Raft achieves consensus in a distributed system.

questions.text: What is a stateless vs. stateful service?
questions.referenceAnswer: Stateless services don't retain client data between requests; stateful services maintain client state, useful for sessions and transactions.

questions.text: Design a large-scale distributed cache system.
questions.referenceAnswer: Consider consistency, data partitioning, eviction policies, and fault tolerance in distributed caching.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Security Design
persona: Formal, exacting head of security engineering.

questions.text: Explain the principles of least privilege and defense in depth.
questions.referenceAnswer: Least privilege limits access rights; defense in depth layers security. Both minimize attack surfaces and provide redundancy.

questions.text: Design a secure and scalable authentication system for a web application.
questions.referenceAnswer: Implement OAuth for third-party integrations, use JWT for stateless authentication, and ensure protection against common security vulnerabilities.

questions.text: Discuss the importance of security in API design.
questions.referenceAnswer: API security is vital to protect data and prevent unauthorized access, using authentication, validation, rate limiting, and encryption.

questions.text: Design a fraud detection system for online transactions.
questions.referenceAnswer: Use machine learning for anomaly detection, implement rule-based systems for known fraud patterns, ensure real-time processing.

questions.text: Design a secure mobile payment system for developing countries.
questions.referenceAnswer: Focus on security protocols, offline capabilities, user authentication, and low-resource optimizations.

title: Senior Data Engineer - Pipelines and ML Systems

questions.text: Design a data pipeline for processing big data in real-time.
questions.referenceAnswer: Utilize stream processing frameworks (like Apache Kafka, Spark Streaming), ensure fault tolerance, and manage backpressure.

questions.text: Design a system for efficient storage and retrieval of large-scale time-series data.
questions.referenceAnswer: Optimize for write-heavy loads, use time-based partitioning, efficient indexing, and consider data compression techniques.

questions.text: Design a recommendation system for a large e-commerce platform.
questions.referenceAnswer: Use collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, or hybrid methods; consider scalability and real-time processing.

questions.text: Design a system to manage and process Internet of Things (IoT) data.
questions.referenceAnswer: Focus on handling large-scale data influx, real-time processing, data storage, and analytics.

questions.text: Design a scalable image processing pipeline for a photo-sharing app.
questions.referenceAnswer: Implement distributed processing, efficient storage, and consider ML techniques for feature extraction.
